options.content:
# Lower Manhattan in motion

996 yellow-cab trips replayed over the buildings of Lower Manhattan. Each trail is one taxi:
the bright head is where the cab is now, and the tail fades behind it. **Press play on the
map's clock**; drag with the right button to orbit.

The data is the example that ships with deck.gl ([visgl/deck.gl-data](https://github.com/visgl/deck.gl-data/tree/master/examples/trips)),
read in place from GitHub once per visit, into your own browser, where [Chaski](https://github.com/ubica-ecuador/chaski) runs every query on this page. Its timestamps count seconds from an unnamed start, so the
clock runs from 00:00 to 00:41 and says nothing about the real hour. The sample was cut at the
30-minute mark — 279 trips end within ten seconds of it — which is why the count below falls off a
cliff there. **Drag across that curve** to replay only that window of it: the map, its clock and the figures keep just the stretch of each trip inside it.

spec.rawSql:
WITH w AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE) AS lo,
         coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AS hi
),
sel AS (SELECT t.* FROM $trips t, w WHERE t.t_end >= w.lo AND t.t_start <= w.hi),
-- The same GPS points the map draws: only those inside the window.
pts AS (
  SELECT n, p, ts FROM (SELECT n, unnest(path) AS p, unnest(timestamps) AS ts FROM sel), w
  WHERE ts BETWEEN w.lo AND w.hi
),
legs AS (
  SELECT radians(p[2]) AS lat, radians(p[1]) AS lng,
         radians(lag(p[2]) OVER lw) AS lat0, radians(lag(p[1]) OVER lw) AS lng0
  FROM pts WINDOW lw AS (PARTITION BY n ORDER BY ts)
),
clock AS (SELECT s FROM (SELECT unnest(range(0, 2490, 10)) AS s), w WHERE s BETWEEN w.lo AND w.hi)
SELECT (SELECT count(DISTINCT n) FROM pts)                         AS "Trips",
       (SELECT count(*) FROM pts)::BIGINT                          AS "GPS points",
       -- Only the legs driven inside the window, haversine as in the dataset.
       (SELECT coalesce(round(sum(coalesce(2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
          power(sin((lat - lat0) / 2), 2) + cos(lat0) * cos(lat) * power(sin((lng - lng0) / 2), 2))), 0))), 0)
        FROM legs)                                                 AS "Km driven",
       -- A trip's whole duration, for the trips seen in the window.
       (SELECT round(median(t_end - t_start) / 60, 1) FROM sel WHERE n IN (SELECT n FROM pts)) AS "Median trip, min",
       (SELECT coalesce(max(c), 0) FROM (SELECT count(*) AS c FROM clock JOIN sel ON s BETWEEN t_start AND t_end GROUP BY s))
                                                                   AS "Most taxis at once"

-- Pinned to midnight UTC on 1 January 2026, the zone kepler's clock shows,
-- so it reads 00:00 to 00:41.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE) AS lo,
         coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AS hi
),
-- Every trip on the road at some moment of the window.
sel AS (SELECT t.* FROM $trips t, w WHERE t.t_end >= w.lo AND t.t_start <= w.hi),
pts AS (SELECT n, vendor, t_start, t_end, km, unnest(path) AS p, unnest(timestamps) AS ts FROM sel)
-- Only the stretch of each trip inside the window, so kepler's timeline spans
-- the window too: whole trips would stretch it back to their first point.
SELECT 'trip ' || n                     AS trip_id,
       'Vendor ' || vendor              AS vendor,
       to_timestamp(1767225600 + ts)    AS time,
       p[2]                             AS latitude,
       p[1]                             AS longitude,
       round(km, 2)                     AS trip_km,
       round((t_end - t_start) / 60, 1) AS trip_min
FROM pts, w
WHERE pts.ts BETWEEN w.lo AND w.hi
ORDER BY n, ts

spec.title: Taxis on the road
spec.description: Cabs mid-trip at each moment, counted every ten seconds. Drag across it to replay only that window: the map, its clock and the figures keep just the stretch of each trip inside it; the toolbar at the top right clears it.

spec.rawSql:
-- How many cabs are mid-trip at each moment, every ten seconds, by vendor.
-- Always the whole clock: the brush is drawn over it, not applied to it.
WITH clock AS (SELECT unnest(range(0, 2490, 10)) AS s)
SELECT s,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.vendor = 0) AS v0,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.vendor = 1) AS v1
FROM clock LEFT JOIN $trips t ON s BETWEEN t.t_start AND t.t_end
GROUP BY s
ORDER BY s

spec.title: Lower Manhattan in motion

source.sql:
-- deck.gl's own trips example, read once into the viewer's browser: one row
-- per trip. Timestamps are seconds from an unnamed start.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT row_number() OVER () AS n, vendor::INTEGER AS vendor, path, timestamps
  FROM read_json('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/visgl/deck.gl-data/master/examples/trips/trips-v7.json', maximum_object_size = 100000000)
  WHERE len(path) >= 2 AND len(path) = len(timestamps)
),
pts AS (SELECT n, unnest(path) AS p, generate_subscripts(path, 1) AS i FROM raw),
prev AS (
  SELECT n, radians(p[2]) AS lat, radians(p[1]) AS lng,
         radians(lag(p[2]) OVER w) AS lat0, radians(lag(p[1]) OVER w) AS lng0
  FROM pts WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY n ORDER BY i)
),
-- Haversine by hand, on the radius ST_Distance_Sphere uses: calling that would
-- make the browser fetch the spatial extension, seconds for one column.
km AS (
  SELECT n, sum(coalesce(2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
           power(sin((lat - lat0) / 2), 2) + cos(lat0) * cos(lat) * power(sin((lng - lng0) / 2), 2))), 0)) AS km
  FROM prev GROUP BY n
)
SELECT raw.n, vendor, path, timestamps,
       timestamps[1]::DOUBLE AS t_start, timestamps[-1]::DOUBLE AS t_end,
       len(path) AS points, km.km
FROM raw JOIN km USING (n)

-- The footprints and heights that ship beside the trips in deck.gl's example.
-- Each ring is a bare list of [lng, lat]; closed here so it reads as WKT.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT height, CASE WHEN polygon[1] = polygon[-1] THEN polygon
                      ELSE list_append(polygon, polygon[1]) END AS ring
  FROM read_json('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/visgl/deck.gl-data/master/examples/trips/buildings.json', maximum_object_size = 100000000)
  WHERE len(polygon) >= 3
)
SELECT height AS height_m,
       'POLYGON((' || array_to_string(list_transform(ring, c -> c[1] || ' ' || c[2]), ', ') || '))' AS geom
FROM raw

spec.description: deck.gl's taxi-trips example replayed over lit 3D buildings of Lower Manhattan.
